Modern.brandNameRationale: Named for the two botanical varieties of Camellia sinensis — var. assamica (broad-leaf Assam, identified by Robert Bruce in 1823) and var. sinensis (small-leaf Chinese). Treats tea with the varietal precision wine gives to Pinot vs. Chardonnay. 'Var.' is the working botanical abbreviation.
Modern.industrySummary: Specialty tea has been chasing the wellness market with adaptogens, fruit blends, and origin stories that gesture at terroir without naming it. There is room for a modern single-origin label that does for tea what third-wave coffee did for beans — name the variety, the harvest, the lot.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bellocq Tea Atelier (bellocq.com) holds the design-led modern slot. Smith Teamaker (smithtea.com) plays the small-batch peer position. In Pursuit of Tea (inpursuitoftea.com) is the producer-first reference. We sit closer to In Pursuit of Tea, sharper on varietal framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern single-origin tea label that names each tin by botanical variety.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 45. Drinks loose-leaf at home. Owns a kettle with a thermometer. Reads tea the way coffee nerds read coffee. Knows the difference between gyokuro and sencha.
behaviors: Brews by weight and water temperature
Refers to teas by garden and flush

dos: Name the variety, the garden, the flush
Print the harvest date on the tin
Write tasting notes in plain English

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark. Camellia Var. set in a tight modern grotesk, with 'Var.' set smaller and italic, sitting on the baseline like a botanical abbreviation in a herbarium label.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for harvest dates and grades
typography.rationale: The mono carries the field data. The regular carries the brand.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Named for Fujian province — the birthplace of oolong, white tea (Fuding), and Lapsang Souchong (smoked over Masson pine in the Wuyi mountains). The Maison + place-name convention places the brand in the négociant tradition, with a single appellation as its limit. Fujian is a geographic name, not a mark.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury tea has been dominated by Paris and London heritage houses that blend across origins. There is space for a single-province house — sold the way a Bordeaux négociant sells a single appellation.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Lupicia (lupicia.com) holds the Japanese luxury reference. TWG Tea (twgtea.com) plays the Singapore luxury peer. Palais des Thés (palaisdesthes.com) sits in the French heritage middle. We sit closer to a single-appellation négociant, narrower than any of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A luxury tea house structured around a single province's terroir.

targetAudience.primary: 40 to 65. Lives between hotels. Drinks oolong after dinner. Buys 100g caddies, not subscriptions. Has visited Wuyi.

dos: Name the mountain, the village, the maker
Print the harvest year in classical Chinese
Speak in the language of rock oolong

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark. Maison Fujian in a high-contrast classical serif, with a single hand-drawn Wuyi mountain silhouette as the hallmark, used in gold foil on each caddy.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the few digital surfaces
typography.rationale: Canela carries the négociant heritage. Söhne handles the booking confirmation.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Tencha is the shade-grown, de-stemmed leaf that is stone-ground into matcha — the unfinished form before the mill. Single archaic trade word, deeply specific to tea. Names the raw material rather than the powder.
Minimal.industrySummary: Matcha brands have proliferated around lattes, smoothies, and wellness. There is space for a minimal label that sells the leaf in its pre-ground form and grinds to order.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Ippodo (ippodo-tea.co.jp) holds the heritage matcha reference. Marukyu Koyamaen (marukyu-koyamaen.co.jp) is the producer peer. Mizuba Tea (mizubatea.com) sits in the modern minimal slot. We sit further out — leaf only, ground to order.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A matcha label named for the leaf, not the powder.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who drink matcha as a daily practice and grind their own. They want the leaf fresh and the powder fresher.

dos: Ship within a week of grinding

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. Tencha in a single-weight grotesk, all lowercase. The favicon is a single small leaf silhouette.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Camellia sinensis is the genus, named by Linnaeus in 1753 for the Jesuit botanist Georg Kamel. Mercantile signals the old tea-clipper trade. The pair reads as a serious B2B tea house already on the panel at restaurants and hotels.
Corporate.industrySummary: Foodservice tea is dominated by mass-market tea-bag brands and a few specialty wholesalers. The opening is for a B2B house that sells loose-leaf by the kilo with the botanical name on every label.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Harney & Sons Wholesale (harney.com) holds the institutional reference. Tea Forte (teaforte.com) plays the hospitality peer. Numi Organic Tea (numitea.com) sits in the foodservice middle. We sit smaller, focused on bulk loose-leaf for serious operators.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A B2B tea house for restaurants and offices, priced by the kilo.

targetAudience.primary: Beverage Directors at restaurant groups, hotel F&B leads, and office coffee buyers managing tea programs across 5 to 500 locations.
behaviors: Sign annual contracts by the kilo
Spec teas by grade and origin

dos: Be clear about grade and price
Print the botanical name on every label
Speak to the buyer, not the drinker

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single Camellia leaf reduced to two strokes. Reads cleanly on a uniform, a delivery carton, and an email signature.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly trade catalogs
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean. The serif reserved for printed B2B documentation.

Creative.tagline: One pot, one leaf, every month.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The kyūsu is the side-handled Japanese teapot used for sencha and gyokuro — the vessel that defines Japanese leaf service. Club closes it as a subscription. The pair reads as a creative tea club for Japanese leaf, pairing the pot with the leaf and the temperature.
Creative.industrySummary: Tea subscriptions have been dominated by sampler boxes with too many bags and not enough leaf. There is room for a creative club that pairs the pot with the leaf and treats temperature as part of the gift.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Ippodo Tea (ippodo-tea.co.jp) holds the heritage Japanese leaf reference. Bird & Blend (birdandblend.com) plays the subscription peer position. Sazen Tea (sazentea.com) sits in the considered Japanese middle. We sit smaller and more curated.
Creative.positioningStatement: A monthly leaf-tea club that ships the pot with the leaf.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 50. Drinks loose-leaf at home. Owns at least one kyusu. Wants someone to choose the next garden for them.
behaviors: Saves the cards from each shipment

dos: Name the garden and the picker
Print the water temperature on the card

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small hand-drawn kyusu silhouette. Kyusu Club set in a friendly modern serif, with the kyusu icon doubling as the favicon and the wax seal on each shipment card.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and shipment cards
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the editorial care of the curation. Söhne handles the digital.
